About the IMAGINE Team

A global network of neuroscientists, physicists, and engineers collaborating to democratize MRI hardware education and development.

Contributors & Researchers

Below is the core research and development group behind the IMAGINE hardware plans and training resources, listed in CITATION.cff:

Dr. Udunna Anazodo

Lead Investigator & Neuroscientist The Neuro (Montreal Neurological Institute), McGill University

Dr. Anazodo leads the IMAGINE initiative. Her research focuses on making MRI technology globally accessible and sustainable, particularly for underserved populations in Sub-Saharan Africa and beyond.

Maureen Nayebare

Lead Researcher & Workshop Instructor McGill University / CAMERA

Maureen has led multiple hands-on construction and training workshops across Montreal (MNI, Douglas, MGH, Polytechnique). Her work spans RF coil prototyping and open science education.

Marina Fernández-García

RF Systems Engineer CAMERA / European Collaborators

Specializes in radiofrequency hardware design, tuning, matching, and active transmit-receive switch development for low-field MR applications.

Haile B. Kassahun

Electromagnetics & Gradient Optimization Engineer Mbarara University of Science and Technology

Author of gradient design research. Focuses on wire optimization and CAD modeling of gradient formers using finite element methods.

Guillermo Sahonero-Alvarez

MR Physics & Systems Integration Developer CAMERA / South American Partners

Responsible for pulse sequence programming and hardware-software system integration on the MaRCoS platform.

Sipan Hovsepian

Robotics & Automation Developer The Neuro, McGill University

Developer of the automated three-axis magnetic field mapping robot (Field Mapper Robot) used for B0 field homogenization and shimming.

Timon Machtelinckx

Magnet Designer & GA Developer CAMERA / European Partners

Developer of the Halbach Array Genetic Algorithm optimization code, enabling automated optimization of ring arrays for homogeneous field profiles.

Dr. Johnes Obungoloch

Senior Biomedical Engineer & Advisor Mbarara University of Science and Technology (MUST), Uganda

A key CAMERA member who has co-led on-site educational workshops in Uganda, supporting hardware replication and training programs.

Stefan du Plessis

Biomedical Systems Coordinator CAMERA / South African Collaborators

Organizes training workshops and oversees system assembly verification in South African partner sites.

OSI² Standard Compliance

10 / 17 OSI² Hardware Score

OSI² CAB Review Checklist

This checklist tracks compliance with the Open Source Imaging Initiative (OSI²) hardware documentation best practices. It helps ensure that researchers and engineers globally can replicate the scanner designs reliably.

1. Readme & Documentation

  • README File Available (1 point) Project description is clearly documented in the repository.
  • Design Considerations Explained (1 point) Detailed design objectives, bore diameter, and magnet configurations are explained.

2. Bill of Materials

  • BoM Provided (1 point) BOM files are available with complete lists of electronic, RF, and magnet components.
  • BoM Best Practices Compliant (1 point) Includes links to DigiKey/Amazon, pricing estimation, and vendor references.

3. Source & Native CAD Files

  • Native Source Files Available (1 point) Autodesk Inventor (.ipt, .iam) and CAD source files are available in the repository.
  • Editable with Open-Source Software (1 point) Files are exportable and editable in FreeCAD / OpenSCAD, and circuits in KiCAD.

4. Production & Fabrication Files

  • Accessible Exports Available (1 point) STEP/STP and 3D printing STL files are provided for direct printing of the magnet rings and RF coil.
  • Manufacturing Environment Defined (0 points) Specific machine/printer settings (infill, filament types, layer height) are currently undefined.

5. Assembly Guidance

  • Assembly Guide Available (1 point) Step-by-step instructions are provided, supplemented by assembly guide animation videos.

6. Development Tracking & Community

  • Versioning Scheme Implemented (1 point) A GitHub Git repository tracks all design changes and history.
  • Public Issue Tracking (0 points) GitHub Issues are not yet utilized actively for bug reports and enhancements.
  • Public Communication Space (0 points) A forum, Slack/Discord workspace, or open email list is not yet linked for developer-user exchange.

7. Testing & Verification

  • Testing Routines Available (1 point) Calibration procedures are provided, such as RF Switch VNA measurements and RF Coil tuning guides.
  • Testing Routines Complete (0 points) Detailed testing guides for the control system enclosure and GPA-FHDO are still in development.

8. Use & Safety

  • User Manual (0 points) A complete end-user manual for running preclinical scans is not yet published.
  • Risk Assessment & Safety Notice (0 points) Safety notices concerning high magnetic fields (B0) and RF power have not yet been formalised.
  • Replication History Documented (1 point) Success stories of independent builds (ERNIE 1 and ERNIE 2) are documented in detail.

IMAGINE Project

An open-source preclinical MRI initiative of the Consortium for Advancement of MRI Education and Research in Africa (CAMERA). Sustaining diagnostic health equity globally.

Open Science Compliance

All hardware files are released under open-source hardware licenses. This project is developed to satisfy the requirements of the Open Source Imaging Initiative (OSI²).
